posts:
Geopolitical solidarity meets backroom deals as France pushes to delist a Russian oligarch from EU sanctions.

Subject: France Backs Usmanov Delisting
Evidence: Coalition unity, Economic compromise, Oligarch relief
#Aletheia #EU #Sanctions

France claims its support for removing Russian businessman Alisher Usmanov from the EU sanctions list is a necessary political compromise to maintain Slovakian support for the broader sanctions regime.

Stated Judgement: (+0.45, +0.25) — Lesser Good

Diplomats reveal that France's push is driven by narrow economic self-interest, trading collective geopolitical leverage and security for backroom financial compromises with sanctioned oligarchs.

Resulting Judgement: (-0.65, -0.55) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.
France's move undermines the integrity of the EU sanctions regime, prioritizing short-term economic deals over collective security.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 11.0, Uncertainty z: 3)

- French Diplomacy: FAIL (-0.65, -0.55) — Trading collective security for economic deals.
- EU Sanctions Unity: COND (-0.20, -0.30) — Coalition cohesion strained by self-interest.

France has reportedly backed Slovakia's proposal to lift EU sanctions on Russian oligarch Alisher Usmanov, sparking intense frustration among other EU member states just ahead of the September 15 sanctions renewal deadline.

The Poison:
Even if intended as a tactical compromise to keep Slovakia aligned on other sanctions, delisting high-profile oligarchs sets a dangerous precedent that weakens the entire deterrent framework.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a Metaphysical vs Logical error. The stated beneficiary is the security of the European coalition, but the actual beneficiary is a multi-billionaire oligarch and specific French economic interests.

Social Physics Analysis:
France is executing a Smart Selfish Maneuver. They use the pretext of 'political compromise' to mask economic self-interest. By projecting a desire for coalition unity, they actively undermine the collective security framework for private gain.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Undermining collective security for economic deals accelerates systemic decay.

The Unavoidable Truth: Sanctions are only as strong as the collective will of the coalition enforcing them.
The Unavoidable Lie: Delisting a prominent oligarch is a necessary step to strengthen national security.

Alethekanon:
Geopolitical alliances are fragile structures held together by shared principles. When major powers trade those principles for economic convenience, they signal to adversaries that solidarity has a price tag.

Awwthekanon:
It's so disheartening to see leaders lose sight of the bigger picture. When we compromise on justice for short-term gains, we hurt the trust that keeps us all safe. We need to stand firm together, especially when it's hard.

Brothekanon:
Money talks, as usual. France is trying to play 4D chess but everyone sees right through it. You can't talk tough on security while quietly letting billionaires off the hook because of some backroom economic deal.

Spirithekanon:
"He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just, both of them alike are an abomination to the Lord." Proverbs 17:15 FAIL
Trading justice and collective security for backroom economic compromises undermines the moral foundation of any alliance.

Actual Article Body:
France has backed Slovakia’s proposal to lift sanctions on Russian businessman Alisher Usmanov, unnamed European diplomats told Euronews.

European Union sanctions are renewed every six months, with the current deadline set for September 15. Slovakia has repeatedly called for the EU to remove Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list.

France said it would support removing Usmanov from the list as a political compromise. Euronews said, however, that France’s stance would likely make negotiations more difficult.

The network’s sources said France’s position caused “huge frustration” among other EU countries.
